steps.title: Open the tape cockpit
steps.narration: This is Tapeology's single-screen cockpit for reading one stock's live order flow. Top-left is the wordmark, the center is where you type a ticker and press Watch, and a status dot top-right honestly tracks whether the stream is live or closed.
steps.point_out: The 'idle' status and the 'No ticker watched' empty state — nothing is being watched yet.

steps.title: Type the buyer-driven sample
steps.narration: We start with the built-in sample stock SIM-BUYER, where aggressive buying is genuinely lifting the price.
steps.point_out: The ticker field now reads SIM-BUYER, ready to watch.

steps.title: Buyers are in control
steps.narration: Press Watch and the cockpit fills with a live read — quote, recent trades, named measurements, observations and an event log — and calls 'Buyer Control' in green with a confidence score, because the aggressive buying is actually moving the price up.
steps.point_out: The green 'Buyer Control' headline with its confidence bar, and all six panels populated live without any page reload.

steps.title: Now the seller-driven sample
steps.narration: Next we watch SIM-SELLER, the mirror case where heavy selling is pushing the price down.
steps.point_out: The ticker field now reads SIM-SELLER.

steps.title: Sellers are in control
steps.narration: The cockpit recognises sellers are in control and shows 'Seller Control' in red — but only because the selling is genuinely driving the price lower.
steps.point_out: The red 'Seller Control' headline; the price is actually falling on the sell prints, which is what earns the directional call.

steps.title: The same heavy selling — absorbed
steps.narration: Now the headline new read. SIM-BIDABS has the very same heavy selling as SIM-SELLER, but here the bid keeps refreshing and the price refuses to fall.
steps.point_out: The ticker field now reads SIM-BIDABS.

steps.title: Bid Absorption, not Seller Control
steps.narration: Because the price holds despite the selling, Tapeology calls 'Bid Absorption' in amber — heavy selling is being quietly absorbed, not winning. Reading price impact over raw aggression is the whole reason this product exists.
steps.point_out: The amber 'Bid Absorption' headline; the new Absorption score / Bid refresh score / Ask refresh score rows in Features; and the event-log lines 'Large sell print absorbed' and 'Bid refreshing at 100.00'.

steps.title: The buy-side mirror
steps.narration: SIM-ASKABS is the mirror case: heavy aggressive buying into an offer that holds firm.
steps.point_out: The ticker field now reads SIM-ASKABS.

steps.title: Ask Absorption, not Buyer Control
steps.narration: The ask holds and the price stalls instead of rising, so the call is 'Ask Absorption' in amber — heavy buying being absorbed rather than lifting the tape.
steps.point_out: The amber 'Ask Absorption' headline and the elevated Ask refresh score that justifies the call.

steps.title: Try an unknown ticker
steps.narration: Finally, a trust check: we type a ticker the system doesn't recognise.

steps.title: It refuses to fabricate data
steps.narration: Instead of inventing a reading, Tapeology shows a clear error and stays idle — it never fabricates a tape state for a stock it doesn't know.
steps.point_out: The red 'is not a known simulated ticker' message, with the status still 'idle' and no fake panels populated.
